channel.title: Boulder City Review
channel.description: Your News from Boulder City Review

item.title: Lady Eagles’ golf team takes regional championship
item.dc:creator: News Engin
item.description: Dominating the field, Boulder City High School girls golf won the 3A Southern regional championship on Oct. 8 at Aliante Golf Club.

item.title: Adventure Center opens its doors
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland Boulder City Review
item.description: It’s been nearly two decades since Boulder City Chamber of Commerce CEO Jill Rowland Lagan first brought up the concept of having a one-stop shop for outdoor adventures.

item.title: Two ballot questions to be decided
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland Boulder City Review
item.description: Whether it’s by mail-in, early or in-person voting the day of this year’s general election, Boulder City voters will be asked to cast their ballots for an array of elected seats. In addition, there will be a pair of ballot questions seeking a yay or nay vote.

item.title: Falling water levels bring submerged B-29 closer to surface at Lake Mead
item.dc:creator: Caitlin Lilly
item.description: The wreckage of a B-29 Superfortress that was once accessible only to advanced divers has moved closer to the surface due to changing water levels at Lake Mead.

item.title: City continues talks with zipline company
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland Boulder City Review
item.description: If all goes well, those near Bootleg Canyon could soon see people flying through the air with the greatest of ease. That or hanging on for dear life and screaming at the top of their lungs.

item.title: ‘Nevadans can’t drink tax dollars’: Voters uneasy on data centers, water ahead of election
item.dc:creator: Alan Halaly
item.description: A new poll shows that a majority of Nevadans are worried about growth’s connection to water resources as well as the proliferation of data centers.

item.title: On-the-job training
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland/Boulder City Review Boulder City Fire Department recruit Eric Benitez assists 7-year-old Benji Hein with a firefighter drill designed for kids during Saturday’s annual pancake breakfast hosted by the Boulder City Firefighters Association. See additional photos on page 3.
item.description: Ron Eland/Boulder City Review

item.title: Oh, what a night
item.dc:creator: News Engin
item.description: Last Tuesday night, hundreds turned out for the city’s annual National Night Out at Veterans Memorial Park. There, attendees were treated to law enforcement demonstrations, prize drawings, free hamburgers from In-n-Out, games for the kids and the popular BCPD vs. BCFD softball game, which the fire department won.

item.title: Tennis teams seek state titles
item.dc:creator: Robert Vendettoli Boulder City Review
item.description: Continuing to be the gold standard in 3A tennis, both Boulder City High School tennis programs captured regional championships over the weekend.

item.title: Library Happenings
item.dc:creator: News Engin
item.description: The following are classes, events and programs available at the Boulder City Library in October.

item.title: New St. Jude’s CEO welcomes opportunity, challenges
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland Boulder City Review
item.description: It’s been about three weeks since Marissa Shoop took over the helm as CEO of St. Jude’s Ranch for Children and according to her, it couldn’t have started much better.

item.title: History comes alive at annual Chautauqua
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland Boulder City Review
item.description: Take a step back in time to the early days of the United States as the country celebrates its 250th anniversary.

item.title: Eagles suffer loss to league rival
item.dc:creator: Robert Vendettoli Boulder City Review
item.description: Boulder City High School football fell to 2-2 on the season, losing their league opener to rival Moapa Valley, 48-13, on Oct. 2.

item.title: Lady Eagles continue to roll
item.dc:creator: Robert Vendettoli Boulder City Review
item.description: Advancing to 7-1-3 on the season, Boulder City High School girls soccer defeated The Meadows this past week, while tying with Equipo Academy.

item.title: Soccer team begins to turn season around
item.dc:creator: Robert Vendettoli Boulder City Review
item.description: Starting to turn the season around in the second half, Boulder City High School boys soccer tied with a pair of league opponents this past week.

item.title: Look out ahead
item.dc:creator: News Engin
item.description: Ron Eland/Boulder City Review file photo

item.title: Fall is in full swing at Garrett
item.dc:creator: Melanie Teemant Principal, Garrett Junior HIgh
item.description: The past few weeks have been busy at Garrett Junior High School as students have continued to settle into the school year, participate in fall activities, and work toward finishing the first quarter strong.

item.title: Council approves rate hike
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland Boulder City Review
item.description: Beginning this month, Boulder City residents will see a bump in their power bills.

item.title: BC Review wins six state awards
item.dc:creator: BCR staff
item.description: During Saturday’s Nevada Press Foundation’s annual Awards of Excellence, the Boulder City Review came away with six awards in the rural category during a ceremony at Springs Preserve in Las Vegas.

item.title: Lady Eagles remain in second place in league play
item.dc:creator: Robert Vendettoli Boulder City Review
item.description: Bouncing back from their first league defeat of the season, Boulder City High School girls soccer added a pair of wins this past week to build some momentum.

item.title: Election 2026: Boulder City candidates answer questions
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland Boulder City Review
item.description: Six Boulder City residents are seeking either reelection or to become a new face on the Boulder City Council dais.

item.title: Best of the Wurst
item.dc:creator: News Engin
item.description: Ron Eland/Boulder City Review

item.title: The view from the hallway
item.dc:creator: Amy Wagner Principal, BCHS
item.description: September is always a busy month at Boulder City High School.

item.title: Country Store celebrates 79th year
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland Boulder City Review
item.description: For nearly eight decades, Grace Community Church has been the place to find that sought-after knick-knack, holiday decoration or maybe a shirt or blouse, all at a discounted price.

item.title: Cozy fall décor that works in the desert
item.dc:creator: Norma Vally
item.description: That first day I feel a little fall chill, I always chuckle to myself thinking about the “sweata weatha” exchange between Maya Rudolph and Amy Poehler from their SNL sketch. While much of the country is pulling on sweaters, downing pumpkin lattes, and decorating for fall, we’re still wearing flip-flops and kicking on the AC.

item.title: BLM asks judge to set aside Boulder City data center approval
item.dc:creator: Alan Halaly
item.description: The agency is asking a judge to set aside its unprecedented approval so it can conduct more analysis of the controversial project. It comes weeks after the judge halted construction.

item.title: My visit with Mickey and the gang
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland
item.description: Walt Disney once said, “I think what I want Disneyland to be most of all is a happy place - a place where adults and children can experience together some of the wonders of life, of adventure, and feel better because of it.”

item.title: Ten inducted into Eagle HOF
item.dc:creator: Ron Eland Boulder City Review
item.description: There’s a saying among many Boulder City High School alumni and that’s, “Once an Eagle, always an Eagle.”

item.title: BCHS 2-1 after homecoming win
item.dc:creator: Robert Vendettoli Boulder City Review
item.description: Picking up a huge homecoming victory, Boulder City High School football defeated 4A Sierra Vista 24-19 on Sept. 18.

item.title: Lady Eagles have their eye on the prize
item.dc:creator: Robert Vendettoli Boulder City Review
item.description: Sweeping their way through league play, Boulder City High School girls golf won their fifth league match of the season at Sienna on Sept. 16.
